title: Seattle weekly community-initiated police calls for service
brief: Revision 2. This round predicts how many calls Seattle residents make to the police in one Monday-to-Sunday week: 911, non-emergency phone, text and in-person calls, counted as distinct dispatch events in the Seattle Police Department's open Call Data (Socrata 33kz-ixgy). The owner's reviewer has settled all three question decisions. Count: community-initiated calls only. Zero point: the 4-week year-over-year reference, built from settled weeks. Before the first scored lock on Sun 2026-12-13 23:59 PT: a two-week unscored pilot of daily archived snapshots. Nothing is left open that blocks approval. Reviewer decision for maintainers: the rights verdict. The card proposes 'approved' on the city's public-domain licence and Open Data Policy OD-1 §D/§E (see Source). Card approval is the owner's sign-off on the question rules; rights confirmation happens at PR review.
question: How many community-initiated police calls for service (distinct CAD events received by 911, non-emergency telephone, text message or in-person complaint) will the Seattle Police Department log with an original queue time in the target Monday 00:00 to next Monday 00:00 week, Seattle local time?

source.publisher: Seattle Police Department, published on the City of Seattle Open Data Portal (cos-data.seattle.gov). Contact listed in the dataset metadata: open.data@seattle.gov [verified 2026-11-08].
source.access: Socrata SODA endpoint https://cos-data.seattle.gov/resource/33kz-ixgy.json. No key, no app token and no account [verified: unauthenticated aggregate queries returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-08 between 22:04Z and 22:11Z; 8-14 s per grouped query]. Daily fetch, once a day, and the archived file. This is the same file during the pilot and in live rounds. The request is GET .../resource/33kz-ixgy.json?$select=date_trunc_ymd(cad_event_original_time_queued) as d, call_type, count(distinct cad_event_number) as n&$where=cad_event_original_time_queued >= '<fetch day - 420 days>T00:00:00'&$group=d, call_type&$order=d, call_type&$limit=50000. 420 days covers the baseline's furthest reach, 399 days before the target week, plus margin. The body is written exactly as served to sources/seattle_cad/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json, one file per day, with url, fetched_at, sha256, bytes and changed_at recorded in sources/manifest.json through ssa/provenance.py (docs/sources.md §4). That gives about 3,000 rows (about 140 KB) a day [inferred from the 2-year body of 253 KB]. The same archived body supplies the lock-time reference, the outage checks, the pilot comparison and the resolution. The live endpoint cannot be read as of a past date, so the archive is the resolution source (docs/sources.md §1.2). Do not register an app token. Fetch once, never in a retry loop (lesson 5). The refresh runs on datacenter runners and that route is untested from here. A 403 or 429 on the first pilot day means a local courier is needed (lesson 3).
source.archive_policy: Use: allowed. Automated retrieval: allowed by intent, inferred. Redistribution of archived bodies: allowed. Evidence: (a) dataset metadata licenseId PUBLIC_DOMAIN, license name 'Public Domain', attribution 'City of Seattle' [verified, api/views/33kz-ixgy.json fetched 2026-11-08T22:03:57Z]. (b) City of Seattle Open Data Policy OD-1 v1.0 (2016-02-01) §D: datasets on the portal 'shall be made available without registration requirement, license requirement or restrictions on their use', except that the city may require a third party to 'explicitly identify the source and version of the public data set, and a description of any modifications'. §E: 'An open license on a dataset signifies there are no restrictions on copying, publishing, further distributing, modifying or using the data for a noncommercial or commercial purpose' [verified, seattle.gov/documents/Departments/Tech/OpenData/COS_OpenDataPolicy.pdf fetched 2026-11-08T22:08:33Z]. (c) The policy says data is published 'in machine-readable format' to support 'automated discovery mechanisms'. No clause against bots or scraping was found in it [verified text]. Reading that as permission for API retrieval is an inference [inferred]. The portal operator's own platform terms (Tyler/Socrata) were not checked [unverified]. Condition to meet: cite 'City of Seattle / Seattle Police Department, Call Data (33kz-ixgy)' with the snapshot date, and say the archive is unmodified. Proposed arena inventory row: rights 'approved', pending the maintainers' decision at review. The agent does not grant it.

target.population: Calls for service that originate with members of the public: CAD events whose call_type is one of '911', 'TELEPHONE OTHER, NOT 911', 'TEXT MESSAGE' or 'IN PERSON COMPLAINT' (owner decision, rev 2). Excluded: 'ONVIEW' and 'PROACTIVE (OFFICER INITIATED)' (officer activity), 'ALARM CALL (NOT POLICE ALARM)' (automated alarm companies; owner confirmed the exclusion, rev 2), and 'SCHEDULED EVENT (RECURRING)' and 'HISTORY CALL (RETRO)' (administrative). The list is frozen at season start. A call_type value not on either list is excluded from the count and logged. Citywide; no geographic split in the regular tier.
target.window: Monday 00:00 inclusive to the following Monday 00:00 exclusive, Seattle local time, on cad_event_original_time_queued. Weeks that contain a DST change have 167 or 169 hours and are counted as published.
target.calculation: Sum over the seven target days of count(distinct cad_event_number) for the included call_type values, read from the resolution snapshot. cad_event_original_time_queued is a Socrata floating timestamp. It is taken as Seattle local time because the hourly profile bottoms out at 05:00 and peaks at 16:00 [inferred from one week, 2026-10-26 onward]. Use distinct event numbers, never rows: the dataset has several rows per event (week of 2026-10-26: 11,591 rows for 6,614 distinct events) [verified]. The per-day, per-type distinct sums equal a direct weekly distinct count for that week: 6,614 both ways [verified for one week only; re-check in implementation].
target.unit: Calls (distinct CAD events) per Monday-to-Sunday week

lock: Sunday 23:59 America/Los_Angeles immediately before the target week, stored in UTC (07:59Z on the Monday in PST, 06:59Z in PDT). This is the arena's rule for behavioural series (season0 note: wikipedia and google_trends 'lock before the measured week begins'). There is no publisher release calendar, so the round text says that SSA both sets this metric and resolves it (docs/sources.md §1.1), and the definition is committed with a timestamp before the first window opens. First scored lock: Sun 2026-12-13 23:59 PT, for the week Mon 2026-12-14 to Sun 2026-12-20; resolution Tue 2026-12-29 12:00 PT. Working back from it: the pilot needs a '+7 days' snapshot of the week of 2026-11-16 to 11-22, which ends Mon 2026-11-23 00:00. That snapshot is the Mon 2026-11-30 archive. The pilot verdict is due Fri 2026-12-11. So the adapter and the first round definition must be on main, with the scheduled refresh running, by Sun 2026-11-29. That is the latest date that still works. One merge to main can carry both and leaves participants 14 days before the lock (lesson 7). If main is reached later, the pilot loses that week and the first scored lock moves to Sun 2026-12-20 23:59 PT, the Christmas week. Before 2026-11-29 the sequence is: owner approval of this revision, the implementation pull request to dev, maintainer review and the dev merge, then the separate dev-to-main merge by its maintainer.
baseline: Ranked zero point, the 4-week year-over-year reference (owner decision, rev 2). Target week starts Monday D; lock is Sunday D-1 23:59 PT. Settled reference weeks: the four Monday-to-Sunday weeks starting D-35, D-28, D-21 and D-14. The week D-7 to D-1, which ends at the lock, is never used, because rows trail the clock by about three days [verified, one snapshot: on 2026-11-08 22:10Z the newest queue time was 2026-11-05 23:59:09]. Ratio of sums: R = (sum of daily counts over the four reference weeks) / (sum of daily counts over the same four weeks shifted back 364 days). Never a mean of weekly ratios. Reference forecast = R x (count for the week D-364 to D-358). All numbers come from the snapshot archived at lock. R, last year's week count and the reference forecast are published and hashed with the question, and later snapshots never change them. The 364-day shift keeps weekdays and weekday-defined holidays aligned (Thanksgiving, MLK, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day). Fixed-date holidays (Christmas, New Year's Day, July 4) fall on different weekdays across years; the question text flags them and the formula does not change. The arena's generic freeze filter (date < lock date) would let the partial week in, so the adapter computes this from whole weeks explicitly. Shown on the board, not ranked: persistence on the week D-14 to D-8. Measured over the 51 target weeks 2025-11-10 to 2026-10-26 (modern backfill, not first prints), for this exact rule: MAE 203 calls (4.26% of the 4,754 mean; median 139, max 641). The persistence reference: MAE 186 (3.91%; median 117, max 951). B beats it in 22 of 51 weeks. R ranged 0.961 to 1.109 [verified computation].
resolution: The first successful archived snapshot at or after Tuesday 12:00 America/Los_Angeles, eight days after the target week ends. Example: target 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-20, resolution snapshot Tue 2026-12-29 12:00 PT. The resolved value is the target week's count from that snapshot. The year-over-year denominator is not re-read: it was fixed at lock. The archived body (bytes, sha256, request URL, fetched_at) is the record. Later publisher revisions, including SPD's full refresh about twice a year [unverified; from the owner's doc], never change a resolved round. Pilot gate before the first scored round (owner decision, rev 2): daily snapshots run from Mon 2026-11-30, and no scored rounds resolve on them. On Fri 2026-12-11 a maintainer compares two weeks. The week of 2026-11-16 to 11-22: its count in the 11-30 snapshot (+7 days) against the 12-11 snapshot (+18). The week of 2026-11-23 to 11-29: the 12-07 snapshot (+7) against the 12-11 snapshot (+11). Go if both weeks grew by less than 0.5% after their +7 snapshot: the 2026-12-13 round is scored with this eight-day resolution. No-go: that round runs unscored, which is announced before its lock, and a new card revision sets a longer lag from the measured growth. The round definition states this condition when it is posted.
missing_data_policy: (1) No successful snapshot by Friday 12:00 PT after the scheduled resolution time: the round is cancelled, never resolved from a later pull. (2) Outage check on the resolution snapshot: if any target day's included count is zero, or below 40% of the median daily count over the 28 days before the target week, the next daily snapshot inside the same grace window is used. If the check still fails at the end of the grace window, the round is cancelled. (3) Reference at lock: if any of the four reference weeks, or their four year-earlier counterparts, or last year's target-aligned week, has a day failing the same outage check, the whole 4-week block steps back one week (D-42 to D-14 and its 364-day shift), and the question text says so. If it still fails, the round is not posted. (4) A call_type value seen for the first time is excluded and logged. If such values exceed 1% of a target week's events, maintainers review the round before it resolves. (5) Pilot snapshots that fail to fetch are recorded as failures and not back-filled. A missing +7 snapshot counts as no-go for that week's comparison. (6) Historical backtests use today's backfill, not first prints, and are labelled that way.
scoring: SSA topline scoring for a predictive distribution over the weekly count: mean and sd (sd > 0) or a quantile map including 0.5, scored with CRPS. Arena target_type continuous_normal. Skill is 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(reference), with the ranked reference being the 4-week year-over-year forecast from the baseline rule. That reference is scored the same way the arena scores its persistence reference today. Because last year's week count is fixed at lock, scoring the count is equivalent to scoring the year-over-year ratio scaled by a known constant (CRPS scales linearly), so this matches the MTA and TSA specs' ratio framing. Also shown, not ranked: skill against persistence on the week two back, median absolute error, and 50%/90% interval coverage. Movement check (arena scoring.noise_floor, last 52 weeks, community calls): noise m = 156, real movement s = 104, ceiling term m/sqrt(pi) = 88. The ranked reference's MAE of 203 is well above 88, so the series is scoreable [verified computation]. An administrative count has no sampling noise, so noise_floor measures week-to-week idiosyncratic variation here. Maintainers confirm whether that reading of the arena score's noise term applies to a count (docs/sources.md §1.4).

evidence.finding: [owner input, not verified] The Seattle spec proposes all CAD events, count(distinct cad_event_number), Mon-Sun Seattle local weeks, previous week's total as baseline, lock Sunday 23:59 PT, resolution Tuesday 12:00 PT after a seven-day lag. It also says the dataset gets a full refresh about twice a year. This card keeps the window, lock, lag and counting rule. It changes the population (decision 1) and the baseline week, because the previous week is not posted at lock. The doc's '11.1 million records' are rows, not events.

Ranking of the doc's datasets on the permission and schedule gates, 2026-11-08. 1 Seattle calls: permission written [verified]; daily, ~3-day lag [verified]; fetch 200. 2 NYC 311: use 'no restrictions' per NYC Open Data FAQ [verified]; automated retrieval and archiving not addressed [unverified]; fetch 200 but 83 s per grouped query; Fri 2026-11-06 was still partial (9,502 vs ~11k). 3 MTA sayj-mze2: Open NY terms allow use 'as you wish' [verified], but a bullet bars access 'by using an automated device, script, bot, spider, crawler or scraper' [verified text; its scope is unclear]. mta.info/open-data returned 403; data fetch 200, newest subway row Tue 2026-11-03. 4 Singapore COE: Singapore Open Data Licence allows 'use, access, download, copy, distribute' [verified]; twice-monthly calendar; keyless fetch 200. But the doc's lock (Monday 16:00 SGT) falls after bidding opens, while live bids are public. 5 BLS CPI rent: API v1 keyless 200 (Sep 450.429); fails the doc's Spatial test (national). 6 NY Fed moving: fastest to launch (arena already archives the SCE workbook; SCE rights approved in ssa/inventory.py) but it measures stated intention. 7 TSA: page 200 to an honest user agent (the doc reported a block); HTML only, and prior-year columns are gone. 8 Zillow: terms bar automated querying (doc) → permission-needed. 9-11 LTA bus and train, carparks: need an LTA DataMall AccountKey (new account), stopped. 12 SG taxis: real-time; SSA would define the metric. Extra doc sections, not among the 12: Texas mixed beverage, OpenTable, Chicago multimodal.

assumptions: Dataset and question picked without asking: Seattle police calls for service, citywide weekly count. Reason: it is the only one of the doc's 12 datasets with machine-readable public-domain licence metadata plus a written city policy covering use, copying and redistribution, and the sample fetch worked keyless. Runner-up 1: NYC 311. Use permission is written ('no restrictions on the use of Open Data'), and it moves more (persistence error 8-10%, more room for skill). But automated retrieval and archiving are not addressed separately, grouped queries take about 80 s, and the shipped example card already covers it. Runner-up 2: MTA subway year-over-year. It is the strongest behavioural series, and the doc's YoY design halves the error (3.0% vs 6.0%). But an Open NY bullet bars access by automated scripts, and its scope needs a reading from the publisher. Runner-up 3: Singapore COE. It has a clear licence and a calendar a year ahead, but it is weak on the doc's Spatial test and its proposed lock falls after live bids are public. Full ranking in the evidence.

Rev 2, owner decisions (Haoyang Shang's reviewer, 2026-11-08). Population A: community-initiated only, alarm calls excluded. Baseline B overturns the agent's recommendation: the ranked zero point is the 4-week year-over-year reference. Reason given: the track principle that seasonal patterns should score roughly zero, consistency with the MTA and TSA specs, and the free holiday credit persistence would give (+12.8% at Thanksgiving, +25.7% at Christmas). Runner-up, A: persistence on the week two back. The agent's original reason for it: more accurate over the year (MAE 186 vs 203) and the arena's standard persistence. A is now shown on the board, unranked. Late arrivals A: a two-week unscored pilot before the first scored lock.

Optional, not blocking: a person may ask the publisher about posting lag in parallel with the pilot; the agent contacts no one. Suggested wording, to open.data@seattle.gov: 'We are building a public research benchmark on the Call Data dataset (33kz-ixgy). Could you tell us how many days after a call is queued it typically appears in the dataset, whether records for past days are added or changed in the daily incremental update, and when the semiannual full refresh happens?' (The reviewer asked for this in open_questions. It sits here because card.py refuses approval while open_questions is non-empty.)

Pilot go/no-go threshold (growth under 0.5% after the +7 snapshot), the Fri 2026-12-11 verdict date and the 420-day query window were chosen by the agent. Reason: 0.5% is about a quarter of the reference's median miss (139 calls, about 3%), so growth below it cannot move a score materially. Runner-up: 1%. Easy to change.

Lock at Sunday 23:59 PT, as in the doc. Runner-up: Friday 14:00 UTC, the time the arena's wiki_top10 weekly rounds use. Reason: both lock before the window. The later lock lets entrants use the weekend weather forecast, which is the response the track wants to reward.

Grace window (3 days, to Friday 12:00 PT) and outage threshold (a day below 40% of its 28-day median daily count) chosen by the agent. Reason: in 766 days of history the lowest ratio was Christmas Day 2025, at 64% (408 calls), followed by Thanksgiving 2025 at 70% [verified computation]. A 50% threshold would sit close enough that a real holiday or storm could be cancelled as an outage, so 40% leaves room for real shocks and still catches empty or truncated loads. Runner-up: zero only. Easy to change.

ALARM CALL (NOT POLICE ALARM) excluded from the community population: 38 events a week, 0.6%. These are automated alarm-company signals, not a resident's decision. Proposed by the agent and confirmed by the owner's reviewer in rev 2. Runner-up: include them.

Regular tier only: a citywide number. A precinct or sector profile (the data carries dispatch_precinct, dispatch_sector and dispatch_beat) and the special-event tier are left to a later card. Reason: one number first, per skill step 1. Runner-up: a five-precinct profile scored with the energy score.

Suggested arena names, for implementation: tracker 'seattle_spd'; series 'seattle_calls_community_weekly'; adapter ssa/adapters/seattle_cad.py with a fetch_text/parse split; raw archive sources/seattle_cad/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json; round_id 'seattle-calls-<week-end YYYY-MM-DD>'. These are naming choices and change nothing in the rules.
